newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle market quiet, tone firm - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle market quiet, tone firm - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Monday were inactive, but had a firm undertone amid outlooks for strong beef demand, feedlot sources said.

Quick delivery of cattle sold last week suggested that packers were building inventories for expected beef business, they said. Fed cattle prices this week also were seen buoyed by the ability of feedlots last week to regain current status after being backed up the previous week, sources said.
No bids were reported, but they were expected to surface at $63.00 per cwt, unchanged from last week's sales. Cattle owners were pricing cattle at $65.00.

Fed cattle prices also were seen supported by last Friday's USDA monthly Cattle-on-Feed report, which showed marketings in the seven key cattle states at 104 percent of a year ago, reflecting feedlots' adeptness at staying current during May, the sources said.

The strong marketings figure was seen lifting nearby live cattle futures, which also should lend support to cash, they said. However, the report also showed active placements in May at 126 percent of a year ago and record on-feed numbers at 113 percent as of June 1, which could weigh on fed cattle prices in the coming months, they said.
